subject: Technical commitments & deployment outline for AtlasPay integration
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlaspay.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlaspay.io>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / call notes - AtlasPay inference needs

Sean —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick summary from our side so we’re aligned before your team drafts the technical outline: 

- Business goal: embed real-time payment-risk scoring into our checkout flow (sub-200ms p95 per transaction).
- Expected peak: 6k TPS during promos (sustained 1.2k TPS baseline).
- Model: ensemble of a small transformer (6B) + light feature-based scorer; current infra runs the transformer on mixed-precision GPUs with a 4k context for session-level history.
- Data concerns: PCI-scope tokenization required; logs must be forwarded to our secure S3 with 30-day retention.
- Compliance ask: SOC 2 evidence and encryption-at-rest details.

Can you confirm Redwood’s recommended serving topology (single-region vs multi-region), whether KV cache will meet our p95 target, and an initial estimate of committed capacity and lead time? Also please attach the MSA and a mutual action plan we can circulate internally.

—Lena
Director, Product — AtlasPay

--

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlaspay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Technical commitments & deployment outline for AtlasPay integration

Lena —

Appreciate the clear summary. Below is our concise technical commitment and proposed next steps based on what you shared. We’ll follow up with the MSA and MAP PDFs attached.

Key confirmations (high level):
- Latency SLOs: we can target 200ms p95 for the checkout path using our dedicated low-latency profile with continuous batching disabled for that route.
- Throughput/Capacity: recommended initial commit is 8 x A40-equivalent reserved slots (config for mixed traffic) to safely cover baseline 1.2k TPS with buffer; burst to 6k TPS supported with autoscaling to spare pooled capacity but will need a short warm-up for large bursts — we recommend burst policy and pre-warming for known promo windows.
- Model support: Redwood runtime supports the 6B transformer at FP16/INT8 operator paths. We propose serving the transformer with KV caching for session history and a lightweight CPU service for the feature-based scorer, then aggregating scores at the API layer.
- Topology: primary-region (us-west-2) dedicated cluster + optional read-only replica in us-east-1 for DR and geo-failover. We’ll include a simpler single-region deployment if AtlasPay prefers faster time-to-prod.
- Data & compliance: logs can be routed to a customer-controlled S3 endpoint via encrypted transfer; we provide SOC 2 artefacts and a whitepaper on encryption and KMS integrations. Logs/outputs related to PCI data will be tokenized at the application boundary before sending to Redwood.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Technical appendix: Marissa (cc) will send a topology diagram + SLO matrix (slo-matrix.xlsx) and a draft of the deployment topology (topology-draft.png).
2) Commercial: Ben will follow up with an initial pricing table for the committed capacity and burst options.
3) Legal: Sean (me) will attach the MSA and a proposed MAP.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.pdf, MSA-draft.pdf

Is Thursday 12/03 10:00am PT for a 30-min technical deep dive with your infra and security teams workable? If so we’ll invite folks and include the topology sketch for review.

Thanks — Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0129

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlaspay.io>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical commitments & deployment outline for AtlasPay integration

Hi Lena — quick technical notes ahead of Thursday’s call. I’ve attached the SLO matrix and a draft topology. High-level items to review on the deep-dive: 

- Latency specifics:
  - With dedicated low-latency profile and KV caching enabled, expected tail behavior for a 6B model is ~110-140ms p95 for pure model time at 256-token contexts; additional network and aggregation overhead adds ~30-60ms depending on colocated API layer. We’ll need to validate with your real request-size distribution (session history length).
  - If p95 under 200ms is strict end-to-end, we recommend: 1) colocated API + feature scorer on same VPC as inference nodes, 2) reduce batching on checkout route, 3) prefetch KV cache for hot sessions.

- Throughput & autoscaling:
  - Baseline slot sizing: our perf tests show one A40-equivalent slot handles ~140-160 qps for that model profile with small batch sizes. The recommended 8 slots nets ~1.1k-1.3k baseline QPS with headroom. For promo bursts to 6k TPS, combine reserved slots with a burst pool and pre-warm windows.

- Persistence & telemetry:
  - We can ship per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns to your telemetry endpoint; retention is configurable on the Console.

Open questions for your infra/security teams:
- How will AtlasPay perform tokenization of PCI-sensitive payloads today? A short note on that flow will help us confirm the log retention design.
- Are there internal PKI or HSM requirements for KMS integration?

I’ll be prepared to walk through the topology diagram on Thursday.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
